summary: De-AI spec for S333XHUB, the RONSO LLC site and the s333xgod app site. The approved directions (Editorial player, Letter chat, Stage comments, MySpace background, Anton, ghost-silver, translucent chat surfaces) are untouched; this spec removes the tells layered on top of them. Every item is verifiable by opening the file and searching the quoted string. House voice, applied to every rewrite below: short declarative sentences with full stops; no em-dash, en-dash, spaced hyphen or arrow in any fan-facing string (ranges are "5 to 7"); straight quotes and apostrophes everywhere; "the artist" is the app's umbrella noun ("the Artist" as the defined term in legal), "him" allowed only inside Fan Mail, "Mazze" never spoken by the app; no "yet", "hang tight", "All set", "Heads up", "please", "Something went wrong", "welcome", "Oops"; no emoji or text glyphs (checkmark, bullet, star) as state, the dagger stays as the brand glyph; load-failure cards are titled "COULDN'T LOAD [THING]" with sub "Check your connection." and pill "Try again", inline fallback sentences are "Could not [verb] the [thing].", role guards are "Only the artist can [verb]." Recommended order: (1) group 5 legal-content.ts rewrite and regenerate, because the App Store review and Stripe read those pages; (2) group 3 support email and site domain, since the legal text embeds them; (3) group 1 copy sweep, one pass with the dash and curly-quote lint scripts added at the end so it stays fixed; (4) group 2 tokens and shared components; (5) group 4 company site. Two owner decisions are flagged inline and must be made before the legal text is regenerated: the standing ticket refund rule, and whether a piece ships in 5 to 7 business days per order or after the run closes.
root_causes: The copy was written one screen at a time with no house style sheet, so the same idea ended up phrased five ways (RETRY next to Try again, three different 'Reported' lines, eleven different words for a user with no name, 'Could not' next to 'Couldn't' next to 'Can't') and the em-dash habit spread into pushes, chat previews, labels and page titles. Real studios write the rules once and every screen inherits them; that is the difference a sharp reader feels.

Placeholder-era text shipped as final: 'App Store version', 'hang tight', 'on the real app', 'Top 8' on a Top 3 screen, 'Exclusive drop' as a default headline, the database default name 'fan', a personal Gmail as the support address, Resend's test sender and a Supabase function still named 'swift-function'. Nobody did the last pass where you read every string as a stranger would.

Styles were copy-pasted instead of defined once: 24 copies of the same small caps label at nine sizes, five copies of the same floating shadow card on five unrelated things, four different header systems, five different confirm dialogs. Each copy drifted a little, and that drift is exactly what reads as generated. One token file and three shared components remove the whole category.

The legal pages and the app's public site were assembled from a checklist (Stripe's website requirements, Apple's EULA points) rather than written from the product. That is why they name Google for an iPhone-only app, never mention tickets that the app sells, never say who RONSO LLC is, use 'What we sell' and 'Who runs this' as headings, and use Tailwind's default amber for links on a black-and-silver brand.

Error handling prints the database's words instead of yours. Roughly fifty catch blocks show whatever the backend says, so a fan can read 'row-level security policy for table messages' in red on a chat screen, while the good fallback sentences already written for those spots never appear. One helper at the library boundary fixes every site at once.

items.change: Stop rendering raw backend error text; keep the house sentences already written
items.exact:
Add src/lib/fan-error.ts:
  export class FanError extends Error {}
  export function fanCopy(e: unknown, fallback: string): string  // returns e.message only when e is a FanError, UnlockPendingError, PurchaseCancelledError, TicketPendingError or PaymentsNotLiveError; otherwise console.warn(e) and return fallback. Map three raw cases before falling back: fetch TypeError / 'Network request failed' / 'Failed to fetch' -> 'Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.'; 'JWT expired' / PGRST301 -> 'Your session expired. Sign in again.'; 42501 / 'row-level security' -> the caller's fallback (never the raw text).
In lib, every `throw new Error('<house sentence>')` becomes `throw new FanError(...)` (tickets.ts incl. intentError, shows.ts friendly(), moderation.ts paidPostBlockedMessage, fanmail.ts, shop.ts, supabase.ts). Leave every `if (error) throw error` alone.
In every screen and component, replace `(e as { message?: string })?.message ?? 'X'` with `fanCopy(e, 'X')`; the existing fallbacks stay as written except where this spec rewrites them. Sites: feed.tsx, chat.tsx, channel/[id].tsx, post/[id].tsx, post-card.tsx, shop.tsx, drop/[id].tsx, ticket/[id].tsx, fan-tickets.tsx, fanmail.tsx, settings.tsx, top8.tsx, reports.tsx, compose.tsx, drop-new.tsx, drop-edit/[id].tsx, show-new.tsx, scan.tsx, gif-picker.tsx.
media-pickers.tsx and media-pickers.web.tsx: log e, then onError('Could not open your photos. Try again.') / 'Could not open your videos. Try again.' / 'Could not open your files. Try again.' (never `Photo picker failed: ` + message).
posts.ts upload failure: console.warn the status code, throw new FanError("Upload didn't finish. Try again."). payments.ts RevenueCat catch: console.warn('[payments] RevenueCat:', err.message); throw new FanError('The purchase did not go through.'). payments.ts 'This post has no valid price tier.' -> console.warn('[payments] no product for', post.price_cents); throw new FanError("This post can't be unlocked right now.").
tickets.ts mode-mismatch: `if (__DEV__) throw new Error('Checkout is misconfigured: ...')` else console.error the same sentence and throw new FanError("Checkout isn't available on this version of the app."). Server side stripe-payment-intent/index.ts: the 'Bad request.' / 'Missing show.' fails become fail('Could not start checkout. Try again in a moment.', 400); the key-mismatch fail becomes fail("Checkout isn't available on this version of the app.", 500) with the existing console.error kept.
auth-provider.tsx fallback 'profile fetch failed' -> 'Could not load your profile.'
Leave sign-in.tsx, sign-up.tsx, forgot-password.tsx and auth-errors.ts as they are (already routed through authErrorCopy).

1. 'What this is': `${APP_NAME} is operated by RONSO LLC, a Florida limited liability company ("RONSO", "we"), for the independent artist who releases music as Mazze and S333XGOD ("the Artist"). By creating an account you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. If you don't agree, don't use the app.`
2. 'Who can use it': `You must be at least 17 years old to use ${APP_NAME}. By signing up you confirm you meet this requirement. Accounts are personal. Don't share your login or use someone else's.`
3. 'Your account': `Fan accounts are free. There are no subscriptions. The only things that cost money are one-time post unlocks, show tickets, and pieces from S333XSHOP. You're responsible for what happens under your account. You can delete your account at any time in Settings. The Privacy Policy says what is removed and what is kept.`
4. 'Post unlocks': `Unlocks are one-time purchases made through Apple's in-app purchase system and follow Apple's payment terms. An unlock gives you permanent personal access to that post inside the app. It is not a download, a license to redistribute, or ownership of the music. Refunds for unlocks are handled by Apple under its policies, not by us. If you reinstall the app or switch phones, use "Restore Purchases" to get your unlocks back at no charge.`
5. 'Show tickets' (new): `Some shows sell tickets inside the app. You pay by card or Apple Pay through Stripe, not through the App Store, so this section applies instead of Apple's terms. A ticket is tied to one show and one account, admits one person, and is a QR code under My Tickets that is scanned once at the door. A ticket that has already been scanned or refunded will be refused. Tickets cannot be transferred or resold. The name you give at checkout may be checked against ID at the door. If the Artist cancels a show, or the last ticket sells to someone else while your payment is going through, we refund the full price to the card you paid with. Otherwise tickets are not refundable. Venue rules, including age limits, apply to entry.`  OWNER DECISION: the last two refund sentences state the rule the code enforces today (auto-refund on cancel, sold-out or past show; everything else manual through Stripe). If the owner intends to refund date changes or advance requests, write that rule here instead; the clause must match what will actually be honored.

items.change: Privacy Policy rewritten to admit everything the app handles and name the real processors
items.exact:
PRIVACY_SECTIONS becomes:
0. 'Who we are' (new, first): `This policy is issued by RONSO LLC, a Florida limited liability company ("we"), which operates ${APP_NAME} for the artist releasing as Mazze and S333XGOD ("the Artist").`
1. 'What we collect': `Account: your email address, the display name you choose, and a profile photo if you add one. Using the app: messages, voice notes and photos you send in chat, direct messages to the Artist, comments, reactions and poll votes, fan mail you send and the photo, video or audio attached to it, your notification settings, your block list, reports you file, and a record of posts you've unlocked. Tickets and pieces: the name you give at checkout, your shipping address for a piece, what you bought and its edition number, and Stripe's reference for the payment. Notifications: a device push token if you turn them on. GIF search: the words you type in the GIF picker go to Tenor to return results. We do not collect your contacts or your location, and we do not track you across other apps.`
2. 'How we use it': `To run the app: showing your name on your messages, delivering chat, remembering your unlocks, getting your ticket scanned and your piece shipped, sending only the notifications you've left enabled, and handling reports and blocks. We don't sell your data, and there is no advertising in the app.`
3. 'Where it lives': `Accounts, messages, photos, orders and tickets are stored with Supabase on servers in the United States. Post unlocks go through Apple's in-app purchase system; RevenueCat keeps the receipt record so unlocks can be restored. Shop orders and show tickets are paid through Stripe, which handles your card details. We never see your card number. Push notifications are delivered through Expo's notification service. Fan mail reaches the Artist's inbox through Resend. GIF search runs through Tenor. Each of these companies handles data only to provide its part of the service, not for its own use.`  (If the Tenor key is unset at launch, phrase it 'GIF search, when available, runs through Tenor.')
4. 'Who can see what': `Other fans see your display name, your profile photo if you set one, and the messages you post in chats they are in. If you buy a piece, your display name and edition number appear in that drop's registry, which every member can see. The Artist sees what fans send: the community chat, direct messages, fan mail, and the name and address on any order, so it can be shipped. Your email address is never shown to anyone. For a physical order we give your name and address to the shipping carrier. Beyond that we share nothing, unless the law requires it.`
5. 'How long we keep it': `For as long as your account exists. A message you delete disappears for everyone straight away; a message the Artist removes is hidden but kept for moderation. When you delete your account in the app, your profile, messages, notification preferences, block list and unlock history are erased immediately; if you ask by email, within 30 days. Two things stay: shop orders and show tickets (your name, shipping address, what you bought and what you paid) are kept for as long as tax and accounting law requires, up to seven years, with your account no longer attached to them; and any report you filed stays in our moderation log.`  (Verify 'immediately' against the delete RPC before shipping; the public delete page already claims it. Do not promise a periodic purge.)
6. 'Deleting your account': `In the app, open Settings, scroll to the bottom, and tap Delete my account. Without the app, email ${SUPPORT_EMAIL} from your account's email address, or use the account-deletion page on our site, and we'll delete your account within 30 days.`
7. 'Children': unchanged.
8. 'Changes and contact': `If this policy changes in a meaningful way, we'll announce it in the app. Questions or requests about your data: ${SUPPORT_EMAIL}, or by mail to ${OPERATOR_NAME}, ${OPERATOR_ADDRESS}.`

items.change: Shop Terms name the seller and tell one shipping story
items.exact:
SHOP_TERMS_SECTIONS becomes:
0. 'Who you are buying from' (new, first): `S333XSHOP is run by RONSO LLC, a Florida limited liability company, on behalf of the Artist. Every order is a contract with RONSO LLC. "We" and "us" on this page means RONSO LLC. Pieces are made and numbered by the Artist and shipped by RONSO LLC.`  OWNER: once the Stripe statement descriptor is set (Dashboard > Settings > Business > Public details) to RONSO LLC or S333XSHOP, add one sentence here that matches it exactly. Do not add a shipping city unless pieces really leave from the Miami address.
1. 'What you are buying': `S333XSHOP sells physical, hand-finished collectible pieces made by the Artist in numbered limited runs. Each piece is one of a fixed run (for example, #7 of 50) and runs are never reproduced. Every piece is made to order or in small batches. Minor variations are part of what makes each one unique, not defects.`
2. 'Prices and payment': `Prices are shown in US dollars and include standard shipping within the United States. Payment is processed by Stripe. We never see or store your card details. Applicable sales tax is calculated and added at checkout.`
3. 'Limits and the registry': `Drops are limited to one piece per fan. Your edition number and display name appear in the drop's public registry inside the app. That visibility is part of owning a numbered piece.`
4. 'Shipping': `Pieces ship within 5 to 7 business days of your order. You'll get a notification with a tracking number the moment yours ships. We ship within the United States only. Make sure your shipping address is correct at checkout; packages returned because of an incorrect address can be reshipped at your cost.`  (The parenthetical about pieces still in production is deleted; the drop page cannot say which. If the owner's answer in group 1 is 'made after the run closes', the first sentence becomes 'Pieces ship after the run closes; the drop page shows the run's progress.' and the drop page must show it.)
5. 'Damaged, lost, or wrong items': `If your piece arrives damaged, email ${SUPPORT_EMAIL} within 7 days of delivery with photos of the piece and the packaging.
